message:
Thanks. I'll ask a few quick questions so I can narrow down what you might qualify for. Please answer whichever apply:

1. How many people live in your household, including you? (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or more)
2. Is your child under 5? (yes/no)
3. Is anyone pregnant, or is there a baby under 1? (yes/no)
4. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none, $1-$10,000, $10,000-$20,000, $20,000-$30,000, $30,000-$40,000, $40,000-$50,000, $50,000-$60,000, $60,000-$80,000, $80,000-$100,000, $100,000-$150,000, $150,000 or more)
5. Does anyone get health insurance through a job? (yes/no)
6. Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments? (under $2,000, $2,000-$5,000, $5,000-$20,000, $20,000-$100,000, $100,000 or more)
7. Any other yearly income, such as pensions, unemployment, interest, or child support? (none, $1-$5,000, $5,000-$15,000, $15,000 or more)
8. Is anyone 65 or older? (yes/no)
reply: Three of us. Our youngest just turned three. I'd have to check. About 250 thousand a year. Hard to say. About 5,000 thousand. Around 11 thousand a month. No, we're all in our thirties.

1. Your household earns about $250,000 a year from work, before tax. Is that right? (yes, or give the correct amount)
2. Does your child attend a public school (K-12)? (yes/no)

Thanks, income confirmed at about $250,000 a year. One more thing: does your child go to a public school (K-12)? California serves free meals at all public schools regardless of income, so this matters. (yes/no, or private/homeschool)

summary: California household of 3 (one child, age 3, plus two adults in their 30s; no seniors, no disabilities reported). Household earned income is about $250,000 a year, which is far above the limits for every programme on the list at this household size. Recommend applying for none of: SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, the refundable Child Tax Credit, the ACA premium tax credit, or free school meals. Free school meals in California are universal for public K-12 students, but the child is 3, so that does not apply yet. Some answers were unclear (employer insurance, savings, pregnancy), but none of them would change the result at this income level. Note that the CTC non-refundable part and any state child care or preschool help are outside this list and may still be worth checking with a tax preparer or local agency.
